events.title: University of Constantinople Founded
events.description: Emperor Theodosius II established a major center of higher learning in Constantinople, the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire. It trained officials and scholars in subjects such as grammar, rhetoric, law and philosophy.
events.significance: It is often seen as one of the earliest state-sponsored institutions of higher education. It helped preserve and pass on classical learning in the Byzantine world.

events.title: Lincoln's Cooper Union Speech
events.description: Abraham Lincoln, then a little-known former congressman from Illinois, spoke to a packed New York audience. He argued that the Founders believed the federal government could restrict the spread of slavery.
events.significance: The speech made Lincoln a national figure in the East. It is widely seen as a key step toward his 1860 Republican presidential nomination and election.

events.title: Birth of John Steinbeck
events.description: John Steinbeck was born in Salinas, California. He became one of America's best-known novelists, writing about ordinary people during the Great Depression.
events.significance: His works include The Grapes of Wrath and Of Mice and Men. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1962.

events.title: The Reichstag Fire
events.description: Germany's parliament building in Berlin was set ablaze. Adolf Hitler's government blamed its opponents and used the fire to justify emergency measures.
events.significance: The fire gave the Nazis a pretext to suspend civil liberties and crack down on opponents. It was a pivotal moment in the consolidation of Nazi power.

events.title: 22nd Amendment Ratified
events.description: The 22nd Amendment to the U.S. Constitution was ratified. It limits a president to two elected terms in office.
events.significance: The amendment formalized a tradition set by George Washington. It followed Franklin D. Roosevelt's four election victories.
